## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13761: JetBrains Gradle worktree run configs — delegate project builds to Gradle in worktrees (LOW priority, JetBrains-plugin-specific)

- **What**: JetBrains plugin's Agent Manager worktree feature now supports running project-level Gradle run configurations (delegated to Gradle, e.g. `./gradlew build`) from the worktree popup. Previously only basic shell commands were executable; project-native build tasks required manual terminal invocation. Adds a worktree-scoped run-config picker that surfaces the project's existing Gradle tasks.
- **Why**: Worktree-based agent sessions often need to run the project's build/test/lint tasks (defined in Gradle) to verify changes before PR creation. Forcing users to open a terminal and type `cd /path/to/worktree && ./gradlew test` breaks the Agent Manager's integrated workflow. Surfacing run configs closes the gap.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13761 (feat(jetbrains): run project run configs delegated to Gradle in worktrees)
- **Category**: command (JetBrains plugin UI)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no Agent Manager worktree UI, no run-config picker. This is desktop-IDE-specific build-system integration. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture. (Alexi CLI worktree equivalent is manual: `cd $(ax agent-manager status --worktree <id> --json | jq -r .path) && npm run build`, which is the CLI-native pattern.)

#### 2. Kilocode #13765: JetBrains auto-approve attention badge settling — per-session grace window (LOW priority, JetBrains-plugin-specific)

- **What**: JetBrains plugin's Agent Manager auto-approve feature shows attention badges (spinner for RUNNING, exclamation for PERMISSION, error icon for ERROR) immediately when a session enters one of those states, but badges were flickering when multiple sessions transitioned in the same emission. Fix: hold attention state per session (keyed by session id) for a grace window (likely 500ms-1s based on prior patterns), so rapid state changes settle before the UI updates. Sessions NOT entering attention states publish immediately; only newly-attention sessions wait out the grace.
- **Why**: A session going to ERROR or RUNNING in the same emission as another session entering PERMISSION caused all of them to wait out the grace window, delaying the spinner/icon display unnecessarily. Keying by session id isolates the debounce so one session's state change doesn't stall another's UI update.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13765 (fix(jetbrains): settle attention badges during auto-approve)
- **Category**: command (JetBrains plugin UI timing)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no Agent Manager auto-approve UI, no attention-badge debouncing. This is desktop-IDE-specific state-machine UI polish. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture.

#### 3. Kilocode #13712: JetBrains Agent Manager PR/run status surface — worktree list metadata (LOW priority, JetBrains-plugin-specific)

- **What**: JetBrains plugin's Agent Manager worktree list now surfaces PR status (open/merged/closed) and GitHub Actions run status (pending/success/failure) inline for each worktree, so users can see which agent sessions have already opened PRs and whether CI passed without leaving the IDE. Metadata is fetched via `gh pr view --json state,statusCheckRollup` and cached per worktree.
- **Why**: Without this, users had to open the GitHub web UI or run `gh pr list` in a terminal to check whether an agent's work was merged or still pending review. Inline status reduces context-switching and surfaces CI failures earlier.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13712 (feat(jetbrains): surface PR and run status in the Agent Manager worktree list)
- **Category**: command (JetBrains plugin UI)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no Agent Manager worktree list UI, no inline PR/run-status display. This is desktop-IDE-specific GitHub metadata integration. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture. (Alexi CLI equivalent is manual: `ax agent-manager list --json | jq -r '.[] | .worktree_path' | xargs -I{} sh -c 'cd {} && gh pr view --json state,url'`, which is the CLI-native pattern for checking PR status across worktrees.)

#### 4. Kilocode #13766: JetBrains fork session from worktree editor — snapshot existing session for new agent run (LOW priority, JetBrains-plugin-specific)

- **What**: JetBrains plugin now allows forking a session (creating a snapshot copy) directly from the worktree editor toolbar, so users can branch an agent's conversation without losing the original session. Fork requests are latched per source session (double-click protection), and the fork RPC includes `x-kilo-sse-skip-fork-sync` header to prevent the SSE reader from parsing duplicate sync events per copied message/part. Worktree controller inserts the returned DTO and reloads via `sessionsFor(directory)` instead of clobbering the primary workspace's sessions flow.
- **Why**: Mid-conversation forks enable "what-if" explorations (try a different approach, test an alternative fix) without losing the original agent's progress. Toolbar placement makes it one-click accessible from the worktree editor where users are already reviewing the agent's work.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13766 (feat(jetbrains): fork a session from the worktree editor)
- **Category**: command (JetBrains plugin UI)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no worktree editor toolbar, no fork-session UI. Session forking is a Kilo/Cline session-management feature; Alexi sessions persist to `~/.alexi/sessions/` but have no built-in fork/branch mechanism yet. This is desktop-IDE-specific session UX. Not immediately CLI-portable (would require designing a CLI session-fork command + SSE-skip header support in Alexi's session manager). Keep on radar for future session-management work.

#### 5. Kilocode #13797: JetBrains session dialog card surface styling — raised surface fill (LOW priority, JetBrains-plugin-specific)

- **What**: JetBrains plugin's session dialog cards (likely the Agent Manager session-list or session-detail modal) now fill their background with a "raised surface" style (likely a lighter background color or subtle elevation shadow) to distinguish them from the surrounding UI. Pure visual polish, no functional change.
- **Why**: Flat cards blend into the dialog background, making it harder to parse which session belongs to which worktree in a dense list. Raised surface provides visual hierarchy.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13797 (fix(jetbrains): fill session dialog cards with a raised surface)
- **Category**: command (JetBrains plugin UI styling)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no session dialog cards, no UI styling concerns. This is desktop-IDE-specific visual polish. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture.

#### 6. Kilocode #13800: JetBrains exclude Kilo worktrees from IntelliJ indexing — toggle + async save hardening (LOW priority, JetBrains-plugin-specific)

- **What**: JetBrains plugin adds a settings toggle to exclude Kilo Agent Manager worktrees from IntelliJ's indexing (file-search, code-completion, inspections). When enabled, worktree directories are marked as excluded roots so IntelliJ skips them during index builds, reducing CPU/RAM overhead on projects with many active agent worktrees. Two bugs fixed in review: (1) the save was launched on the configurable's own scope (cancelled by `disposeUIResources()`), so Apply worked but OK silently did nothing — moved save to app-lifetime scope; (2) async fetch landing after user flipped the switch overwrote their choice — added touched-flag to skip refresh when user modified the control.
- **Why**: Agent Manager worktrees are ephemeral Git worktrees (often 10-20 active at once in the fleet setup), and indexing all of them slows down the IDE. Excluding them keeps the primary workspace indexed while skipping the transient agent branches.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13800 (feat(jetbrains): exclude Kilo worktrees from IntelliJ indexing)
- **Category**: command (JetBrains plugin settings + indexing integration)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no Agent Manager worktrees, no IntelliJ indexing integration. This is desktop-IDE-specific performance tuning. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture.

#### 7. Kilocode #13816: GPT-6 Astra OAuth display — show correct model name in ChatGPT OAuth flow (LOW priority, display-label-only)

- **What**: VS Code extension's ChatGPT OAuth flow (device sign-in) now displays "GPT-6 Astra" instead of a stale model name (likely "GPT-5" or generic "ChatGPT") when authenticating against the ChatGPT OAuth provider. Pure display change, no functional impact on provider selection or routing.
- **Why**: Users see the model name during authentication and expect it to match the model they're invoking. Stale labels cause confusion ("am I signing in to the right tier?").
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13816 (fix(cli): show GPT-6 Astra for ChatGPT OAuth)
- **Category**: config (display label)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no ChatGPT OAuth flow, no device sign-in UI, no GPT-6 Astra model integration. This is a display-label-only change to Kilocode's OAuth UI. Not actionable for Alexi (Alexi uses SAP AI Core providers, not ChatGPT OAuth).

#### 8. OpenCode #47385 + #47384: Codex GPT version comparison — integer versions + major/minor compare (LOW priority, console-specific)

- **What**: OpenCode console's Codex model filter (likely a UI picker for selecting OpenAI Codex models) now allows integer model versions (e.g. `gpt-4` instead of requiring `gpt-4.0`) and compares versions by major + minor components only (ignoring patch/build suffixes) so `gpt-4.1` and `gpt-4.1.2` are treated as equivalent. Previously the filter required exact string matches, breaking when model IDs gained patch versions.
- **Why**: OpenAI's model versioning is inconsistent: some models have integer versions (`gpt-4`), others have semver-ish versions (`gpt-4.5-turbo-preview`), and the same model can appear with or without patch components across different listings. Flexible parsing prevents the filter from silently dropping models.
- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/47385 (fix(opencode): compare Codex GPT versions by major and minor), https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/47384 (fix(opencode): allow integer GPT versions in Codex model filter)
- **Category**: provider (model version parsing)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no Codex model filter, no console UI, no OpenAI Codex integration (Alexi uses SAP AI Core providers). This is console-UI-specific model-selection logic. Not CLI-portable. (If Alexi ever adds OpenAI provider support, flexible version parsing would be useful, but that is speculative future work, not an immediate action item.)
